sn12.27:1.2: “Bhikkhus, with ignorance as condition, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.27:1.3: with volitional formations as condition, consciousness …
sn12.27:1.4: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.27:2.2: The aging of the various beings …
sn12.27:2.7: thus this aging and this death are together called aging-and-death.
sn12.27:2.8: With the arising of birth there is the arising of aging-and-death;
sn12.27:2.9: with the cessation of birth there is the cessation of aging-and-death.
sn12.27:2.10: Just this Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of aging-and-death;
sn12.27:2.11: that is, right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
sn12.27:4.2: There are these three kinds of volitional formations:
sn12.27:4.3: the bodily volitional formation, the verbal volitional formation, the mental volitional formation.
sn12.27:4.5: With the arising of ignorance there is the arising of volitional formations.
sn12.27:4.6: With the cessation of ignorance there is the cessation of volitional formations.
sn12.27:4.7: Just this Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of volitional formations;
sn12.27:4.8: that is, right view … right concentration.
sn12.27:5.1: “When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple thus understands the condition; thus understands the origin of the condition; thus understands the cessation of the condition; thus understands the way leading to the cessation of the condition,
sn12.27:5.2: he is then called a noble disciple who is accomplished in view, accomplished in vision, who has arrived at this true Dhamma, who sees this true Dhamma, who possesses a trainee’s knowledge, a trainee’s true knowledge, who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrative wisdom, one who stands squarely before the door to the Deathless.”
